creator: Alexander Terp
description:
A variadic int arg renders `ints` in `--help` where a variadic float
renders `[floats...]`:

```
      --numbers ints
      --values [floats...]
```

The bracket form is what tells a reader the arg takes several values, and
int is the one type that doesn't get it.

Rad registers its int args on ra's `Int64` flags, so ra would name them
`int64` and `int64s` - a width Rad's language has no word for. Rad has
corrected that since the pflag-to-ra switch (043d1047) by hardcoding
`SetCustomUsageType("int")` and `("ints")` in `core/args.go`. A plain
string can't vary with the flag, so the variadic form was never reachable
from there.

`e068dd65` removed every other rad-side placeholder string, leaving these
two as the only ones. `AGENTS.md` is explicit that this is the wrong repo
for the fix: ra owns the table of type names and is the only layer that
knows whether a flag is variadic.

The upstream change is written and tested, sitting unpushed on ra's main
as `85353c1` - it renames `Int64Flag` to `int` and `Int64SliceFlag` to
`ints` / `[ints...]`. Releasing it is the call this card is waiting on:
`IntFlag` and `Int64Flag` would then render identically, which is a real
loss for a consumer displaying both, recoverable with
`SetCustomUsageType("int64")` at the one site that wants the distinction.

Once ra ships, this is a `go.mod` bump plus deleting the two hardcoded
calls, and every arg type forwards its placeholder the same way. Expect
exactly one snapshot line to move: `args/variadic.snap`, `--numbers ints`
to `[ints...]`. More than one means something else changed.

Worth pinning the whole matrix at the same time. `args.snap`'s
`HelpWorksForAllTypes` covers the eight non-variadic types; a variadic
sibling would cover the remaining four, so no type's placeholder can
drift from the rest unnoticed again.
title: Variadic int args render `ints`, not `[ints...]` - needs an ra release
